414	    def _scan_all_chains(self, lines, bad_line=None, exact_fields=False):
415	        # Validate every tenant chain over decoded JSONL lines in one
416	        # physical-order pass, records of different tenants interleaving
417	        # freely. Each tenant gets an independent expected seq and prev
418	        # digest starting at (1, ZERO) on first appearance -- the per-tenant
419	        # rules _scan applies, evaluated for all tenants at once the way
420	        # verify_all does. Returns the parsed records in physical order.
421	        # The first defective physical line raises AuditChainStateError
422	        # directly, with tenant/seq/reason/line filled exactly the way the
423	        # _scan/_Broken path fills them for a single tenant; a line whose
424	        # tenant cannot be determined at all (unparseable, non-object, no
425	        # "tenant" key) reports tenant None and seq None. With
426	        # exact_fields=True a record must carry exactly the five FIELDS keys
427	        # (the import_all input contract); otherwise only missing keys are
428	        # defects, matching the file-scan rule every other entry point uses.
429	        # If bad_line is given, an undecodable physical line follows the
430	        # lines provided; it is reported as missing only when no earlier
431	        # problem was found.
432	        states = {}  # serialized tenant -> [expected_seq, prev_hash]
433	        records = []
434	        for line, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
435	            try:
436	                item = _strict_loads(raw)
437	            except Exception:
438	                raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", line) from None
439	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
440	                raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", line) from None
441	            tenant = item["tenant"]
442	            key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
443	            state = states.get(key)
444	            if state is None:
445	                state = [1, ZERO]
446	                states[key] = state
447	            expected, prev = state
448	            if exact_fields:
449	                malformed = set(item) != set(FIELDS)
450	            else:
451	                malformed = any(k not in item for k in FIELDS)
452	            if malformed:
453	                seq = item.get("seq")
454	                at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) \
455	                    and not isinstance(seq, bool) else expected
456	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, at, "missing", line) from None
457	            seq = item["seq"]
458	            # Same strict JSON-integer seq rule as _scan: 1.0/1e0, bools,
459	            # strings, null, arrays/objects and mismatching integers are all
460	            # sequence defects, so this scan agrees with every other entry.
461	            if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
462	                    or seq != expected:
463	                raise AuditChainStateError(
464	                    tenant, expected, "sequence", line) from None
465	            if item["prev"] != prev:
466	                raise AuditChainStateError(
467	                    tenant, expected, "digest", line) from None
468	            if item["hash"] != self._hash(item):
469	                raise AuditChainStateError(
470	                    tenant, expected, "digest", line) from None
471	            state[0] += 1
472	            state[1] = item["hash"]
473	            records.append(item)
474	        if bad_line is not None:
475	            # First undecodable byte: tenant cannot be parsed, so None.
476	            raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", bad_line) from None
477	        return records

479	    def _scan_import_ranges(self, lines, bad_line, assertions):
480	        # Validate a multi-tenant segmented import byte stream before the
481	        # target is touched. assertions is the fully validated list of
482	        # (tenant, expected_count, expected_hash) tuples in expected_heads
483	        # order; each asserted tenant must appear in the stream at least
484	        # once. Tenants may interleave freely, but every physical line must be
485	        # an object carrying exactly the five FIELDS keys of a tenant named in
486	        # assertions; a record of an unlisted canonical tenant identity
487	        # violates the segmented input contract and raises _ForeignTenant
488	        # (surfaced as ValueError by import_all_range), exactly the rule
489	        # _scan_import applies. Each tenant's seqs run expected_count+1,
490	        # expected_count+2, ... continuously and the first prev equals the
491	        # asserted hash, each digest recomputed. Returns the parsed records in
492	        # physical order. The first defective physical line raises
493	        # AuditChainStateError directly, filled exactly the way
494	        # _scan_all_chains fills it; a line whose tenant cannot be determined
495	        # (unparseable, non-object, no "tenant" key) reports tenant/seq None.
496	        # After every line has validated, a listed tenant with no record is
497	        # still a defect: the first such assertion in assertions order is
498	        # reported as missing with line None. If bad_line is given, an
499	        # undecodable physical line follows the lines provided and is
500	        # reported as missing only when no earlier problem was found.
501	        states = {}  # serialized tenant -> [tenant, expected, prev, seen]
502	        for tenant, count, head in assertions:
503	            states[self._tenant_key(tenant)] = [
504	                tenant, count + 1, head, False]
505	        records = []
506	        for line, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
507	            try:
508	                item = _strict_loads(raw)
509	            except Exception:
510	                raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", line) from None
511	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
512	                raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", line) from None
513	            tenant = item["tenant"]
514	            key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
515	            state = states.get(key)
516	            if state is None:
517	                # A canonical tenant identity no head assertion lists: this
518	                # violates the segmented input contract (surfaced as
519	                # ValueError by import_all_range), the same rule
520	                # _scan_import applies to a foreign single-tenant record. It
521	                # is raised in physical-line order, so an earlier chain
522	                # defect on a prior line still takes priority.
523	                raise _ForeignTenant(line)
524	            expected, prev = state[1], state[2]
525	            if set(item) != set(FIELDS):
526	                seq = item.get("seq")
527	                at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) \
528	                    and not isinstance(seq, bool) else expected
529	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, at, "missing", line) from None
530	            seq = item["seq"]
531	            # Same strict JSON-integer seq rule as every other scan: 1.0/1e0,
532	            # bools, strings, null, arrays/objects and mismatching integers are
533	            # all sequence defects.
534	            if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
535	                    or seq != expected:
536	                raise AuditChainStateError(
537	                    tenant, expected, "sequence", line) from None
538	            if item["prev"] != prev:
539	                raise AuditChainStateError(
540	                    tenant, expected, "digest", line) from None
541	            if item["hash"] != self._hash(item):
542	                raise AuditChainStateError(
543	                    tenant, expected, "digest", line) from None
544	            state[1] += 1
545	            state[2] = item["hash"]
546	            state[3] = True
547	            records.append(item)
548	        if bad_line is not None:
549	            # First undecodable byte: tenant cannot be parsed, so None.
550	            raise AuditChainStateError(None, None, "missing", bad_line) from None
551	        # Every listed tenant must have at least one record in the stream.
552	        for tenant, count, _head in assertions:
553	            state = states[self._tenant_key(tenant)]
554	            if not state[3]:
555	                raise AuditChainStateError(
556	                    tenant, count + 1, "missing", None) from None

559	    def append(self, tenant, event):
560	        # Validate the new input against the standard-JSON boundary before
561	        # anything else: an illegal tenant/event raises ValueError without
562	        # reading history or writing a single byte, and takes priority over
563	        # any append action (including corrupt-history rejection). It is
564	        # deliberately also evaluated before taking the lock, so a malformed
565	        # caller can never be turned into a different outcome by contention.
566	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
567	        _validate_json_value(event)
568	        with self._write_lease() as f:
569	            # The scan and the write happen under one exclusive lease on the
570	            # very file description used for both, so the record is always
571	            # computed from the latest complete state right before its own
572	            # bytes hit disk: competing appends serialize here and each
573	            # observes the previous winner's record already on disk.
574	            data = f.read()
575	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
576	            try:
577	                count, prev = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
578	            except _Broken as b:
579	                seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
580	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
581	            item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1, "event": event, "prev": prev}
582	            item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
583	            # One O_APPEND write places the whole record atomically at the
584	            # current end of the file; under the exclusive lease no other
585	            # writer moves that end, and no existing byte can be overwritten.
586	            prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
587	            record = prefix + (
588	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
589	            ).encode("utf-8")
590	            f.write(record)
591	            return item

593	    def append_batch(self, tenant, events):
594	        # Append a group of same-tenant events as one verifiable interval.
595	        # events must be a list (a bare JSON value, including a string, is
596	        # not a batch); the tenant and every event cross the same standard-
597	        # JSON boundary as in append. All of this is checked before taking
598	        # the lease, so a malformed call raises ValueError without reading
599	        # history or creating the file, under any contention. An empty list
600	        # is a no-op: nothing is created and no existing byte is touched.
601	        if not isinstance(events, list):
602	            raise ValueError(
603	                f"events must be a list, got {type(events).__name__}"
604	            )
605	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
606	        for event in events:
607	            _validate_json_value(event)
608	        if not events:
609	            return []
610	        with self._write_lease() as f:
611	            # One lease covers the whole read-build-append interval, so the
612	            # batch is an indivisible result for competing writers: their
613	            # records serialize wholly before or wholly after these, never
614	            # between two of its records. The records are emitted as one
615	            # byte block at the current end of file, so readers under the
616	            # shared lease likewise see either the whole batch or none of
617	            # it. The first record continues the tenant chain found on disk;
618	            # each later record links to the previous record of the batch.
619	            data = f.read()
620	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
621	            try:
622	                count, prev = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
623	            except _Broken as b:
624	                seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
625	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
626	            items = []
627	            chunks = []
628	            for event in events:
629	                item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1,
630	                        "event": event, "prev": prev}
631	                item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
632	                items.append(item)
633	                chunks.append(
634	                    json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
635	                )
636	                count += 1
637	                prev = item["hash"]
638	            prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
639	            block = prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8")
640	            f.write(block)
641	            return items

643	    def _append_batch_if_head_locked(self, f, tenant, events,
644	                                     expected_count, expected_hash):
645	        # Scan, compare and append on a description already holding the
646	        # exclusive data-file lease. A corrupt history is reported exactly as
647	        # append reports it and the assertion is never evaluated against an
648	        # unverifiable chain; a well-formed but mismatching head is a conflict.
649	        # Nothing is written on either failure path.
650	        data = f.read()
651	        lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
652	        try:
653	            count, head = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
654	        except _Broken as b:
655	            seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
656	            raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
657	        # _scan returns ZERO for an empty chain, so an empty history is
658	        # compared by the exact same rule as a non-empty one: the call
659	        # proceeds only when both the length and the tail digest match.
660	        if count != expected_count or head != expected_hash:
661	            raise AuditChainConflictError(
662	                tenant, expected_count, expected_hash, count, head
663	            )
664	        # Head confirmed. The records use the identical fields, seq numbering,
665	        # prev digest and hash algorithm as append: the first continues the
666	        # asserted chain head, each later one links to the previous record of
667	        # the batch, exactly as append_batch links its records.
668	        items = []
669	        chunks = []
670	        prev = head
671	        for event in events:
672	            item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1,
673	                    "event": event, "prev": prev}
674	            item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
675	            items.append(item)
676	            chunks.append(
677	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
678	            )
679	            count += 1
680	            prev = item["hash"]
681	        # One O_APPEND write places the whole batch atomically at the
682	        # current end of file; under the exclusive lease no other writer
683	        # moves that end, and no existing byte can be overwritten.
684	        prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
685	        block = prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8")
686	        f.write(block)
687	        return items

698	    @contextlib.contextmanager
699	    def _head_lease(self, tenant, expected_count, expected_hash):
700	        # One exclusive lease covering validation-read, head comparison and
701	        # the write of a conditional append. On an existing log that is the
702	        # ordinary data-file lease; before the log exists, the data-file lock
703	        # cannot be taken without creating the path (and a losing assertion
704	        # must leave no file), so the directory lease -- the same one ordinary
705	        # appends hold while creating the file -- guards the whole
706	        # missing-file branch. The existence probe, the empty-chain
707	        # comparison and a winning creation are therefore indivisible
708	        # relative to every other writer. Lock order is always
709	        # directory-then-data, so the nesting cannot deadlock against a plain
710	        # append. _dir_lease also ensures the parent directory exists.
711	        with self._dir_lease():
712	            try:
713	                f = open(self.path, "r+b")
714	            except FileNotFoundError:
715	                # Definitive empty chain for every tenant: no other writer
716	                # can create the path while this lease is held. A non-empty
717	                # assertion is a deterministic conflict and must not create
718	                # the log; only an exact (0, ZERO) assertion may.
719	                if expected_count != 0 or expected_hash != ZERO:
720	                    raise AuditChainConflictError(
721	                        tenant, expected_count, expected_hash, 0, ZERO
722	                    )
723	                f = open(self.path, "a+b")
724	            try:
725	                fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
726	                f.seek(0)
727	                # When the file existed, assertions against the same head
728	                # serialize here: one appends and observes (count, head),
729	                # every other observes the winner's new tail and gets the
730	                # conflict with the actual values, no byte written by a
731	                # losing call. When this call just created the file the scan
732	                # confirms the empty head it was allowed to create for.
733	                yield f
734	            finally:
735	                f.flush()
736	                f.close()

803	        # Cross-tenant atomic append. entries must be a list of objects whose

809	        # is a no-op after validation: no file is created, no history is read
810	        # and no byte changes.

812	            raise ValueError(
813	                f"entries must be a list, got {type(entries).__name__}"
814	            )

816	        for entry in entries:
817	            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"tenant", "event"}:
818	                raise ValueError(
819	                    "each entry must be an object containing exactly the "
820	                    f"keys 'tenant' and 'event', got {entry!r}"
821	                )
822	            tenant, event = entry["tenant"], entry["event"]
823	            _validate_json_value(tenant)
824	            _validate_json_value(event)
825	            norm.append((tenant, event))

827	            return []

829	            # One lease and one consistent snapshot cover the validation of
830	            # every affected chain and the single block write, so the whole
831	            # group commits as one indivisible byte interval: competing
832	            # writers serialize wholly before or after it and shared-lease
833	            # readers observe either the complete pre-commit or the complete
834	            # post-commit state, never a partial group.
835	            data = f.read()
836	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)

838	            # runs (seqs 1..n from a ZERO prev, each digest recomputed);

840	            # raised immediately: when several affected chains are broken,
841	            # the first physical line in the log decides the result, and an
